title: Two-quantifier theory of the local enumeration degrees
formal: Is the universal-existential theory of the Σ⁰₂ enumeration degrees decidable in the pure order language?
definitions:
For sets A,B⊆N, write A≤_e B if there is a computably enumerable set W of pairs (n,F), where F is a finite subset of N, such that n∈A iff some (n,F)∈W has F⊆B. Finite sets are coded by binary characteristic strings. Mutual enumeration reducibility defines an enumeration degree. A set is Σ⁰₂ if membership has the form n∈A iff ∃u∀v R(n,u,v) for a decidable predicate R. The structure here consists of enumeration degrees containing such a set, with the order induced by ≤_e. It is not the structure of all enumeration degrees or that of c.e. Turing degrees.

Input is a finite encoded sentence ∀x1…∀xr ∃y1…∃ys θ, where r,s≥0 are arbitrary finite integers and θ is any Boolean combination of atoms u≤v and u=v in these variables. There are no constants, function symbols or hidden quantifiers. Fix any effective finite-string encoding of formulas; malformed strings may be rejected. Decidable means one ordinary Turing program halts on every input and answers whether the sentence is true in the specified structure; there is no complexity bound.

import_provenance.original_statement: Is the ∀∃ first-order theory of the Σ⁰₂ enumeration degrees decidable, in the language of their partial order? Lempp and collaborators’ work on Ahmad pairs resolves specific configurations needed for such a decision procedure but leaves the general theory.

sentences: Enumeration reductions use positive finite information from an oracle set.
Mutual reducibility identifies sets into degrees.
Only degrees with a Σ⁰₂ representative occur in the local structure.
The input formulas have one universal and one existential block.
The known Ahmad-pair restriction does not decide arbitrary sentences of this form.
